questions.questionHtml:
\[x^{2} = 49\]

Which of the following is a positive solution to the equation above?
questions.explanationHtml: Taking the square root of both sides gives \(x = 7\) or \(x = -7\). The positive solution is 7.

questions.questionHtml:
\[x^{2} - 5x = 0\]

What is the non-zero solution to the equation above?
questions.explanationHtml: Factor: \(x(x - 5) = 0\), so \(x = 0\) or \(x = 5\). The non-zero solution is 5.

questions.questionHtml:
\[|x - 6| = 4\]

What is the sum of the two solutions to the equation above?

\[\begin{cases} y = x^{2} \\ y = 3x \end{cases}\]

The system of equations above has two solutions. What is the positive \(x\)-coordinate of a solution?

\[\sqrt{2x + 3} = 5\]

What is the value of \(x\) that satisfies the equation above?

\[\begin{cases} y = x^{2} - 4 \\ y = 0 \end{cases}\]

Which of the following is a negative solution \((x,y)\) to the system?

\[\frac{x + 4}{x - 2} = 3\]

What is the solution to the equation above?

\[\begin{cases} x^{2} + y^{2} = 100 \\ y = 8 \end{cases}\]

If \(x > 0\), what is the value of \(x\) in the solution to the system?

\[(2x - 1)^{2} = 9\]

What is the smaller solution to the equation?
questions.explanationHtml: \(2x - 1 = 3\) or \(2x - 1 = -3 \rightarrow x = 2\) or \(x = -1\). The smaller solution is \(-1\).

questions.questionHtml:
\[x^{2} + 6x = 0\]

The equation above has two solutions. What is the product of the two solutions?

\[x^{2} - 2x = 15\]

What is the sum of the two solutions to the equation above?

\[|2x - 5| = 7\]

What is the product of the two solutions?

\[\begin{cases} y = x^{2} - 2 \\ y = 2x + 1 \end{cases}\]

The system of equations above has two solutions. What is the sum of the \(x\)-coordinates of the solutions?

\[\sqrt{3x + 10} = x + 2\]

What is the extraneous solution, if any, to the equation above?
questions.explanationHtml: Square: \(3x + 10 = x^{2} + 4x + 4 \rightarrow 0 = x^{2} + x - 6 \rightarrow (x+3)(x-2)=0 \rightarrow x=-3\) or \(x=2\). Check \(x=-3\): LHS=1, RHS=-1, extraneous. \(x=2\) works.

questions.questionHtml:
\[\begin{cases} y = x^{2} - 4x + 5 \\ y = 2x - 3 \end{cases}\]

If the two intersection points are \((x_{1}, y_{1})\) and \((x_{2}, y_{2})\), what is \(y_{1} + y_{2}\)?

\[\frac{x + 4}{x - 2} = \frac{2x + 1}{x + 1}\]

What is the product of the solutions?

\[\begin{cases} x^{2} + y^{2} = 25 \\ y = x + 1 \end{cases}\]

If \((x,y)\) is a solution with \(x > 0\), what is the value of \(x + y\)?

\[x^{2} + 4x + c = 0\]

In the quadratic equation above, \(c\) is a constant. The equation has exactly one real solution. What is the value of \(c\)?

\[\begin{cases} y = (x-1)^{2} + 2 \\ y = k \end{cases}\]

In the system above, \(k\) is a constant. For which of the following values of \(k\) does the system have exactly one solution?
questions.explanationHtml: Parabola has vertex at \((1,2)\). A horizontal line intersects exactly once only at the vertex, so \(k = 2\).

questions.questionHtml:
\[\begin{cases} x^{2} + y^{2} = 40 \\ xy = 12 \end{cases}\]

If \((x,y)\) is a solution to the system above and \(x > y > 0\), what is the value of \(x - y\)?
In the \(xy\)-plane, a line with equation \(y = -2x + k\) intersects the parabola \(y = x^{2} - 4x + 5\) at exactly one point. If \(k\) is a constant, what is the value of \(k\)?
questions.explanationHtml: Set \(x^{2} - 4x + 5 = -2x + k \rightarrow x^{2} - 2x + (5-k) = 0\). Exactly one intersection → discriminant = 0: \(4 - 4(5-k) = 0 \rightarrow 4 - 20 + 4k = 0 \rightarrow 4k = 16 \rightarrow k=4\).

questions.questionHtml:
\[\begin{cases} y = x^{2} - 6x + 10 \\ y = 2x - 6 \end{cases}\]

How many distinct real solutions does the system have?

\[\sqrt{3x + 7} = x - 1\]

What is the solution set of the equation above?
questions.explanationHtml: Square: \(3x + 7 = x^{2} - 2x + 1 \rightarrow 0 = x^{2} - 5x - 6 \rightarrow (x-6)(x+1)=0 \rightarrow x=6\) or \(x=-1\). Check: \(x=6\) works; \(x=-1\) gives LHS=2, RHS=-2, extraneous. Solution set \(\{6\}\).

questions.questionHtml:
\[\frac{2x}{x - 3} = 1 + \frac{6}{x - 3}\]

What is the solution to the equation above?
questions.explanationHtml: Multiply by \(x-3\) (\(x \neq 3\)): \(2x = (x-3) + 6 \rightarrow 2x = x + 3 \rightarrow x = 3\). But \(x=3\) makes denominator zero, extraneous. No solution.

questions.questionHtml:
\[\begin{cases} x + y = 7 \\ x^{2} + y^{2} = 25 \end{cases}\]

If \((x,y)\) is a solution with \(x > y\), what is the value of \(x - y\)?

\[\frac{1}{(x-2)^{2}} - \frac{4}{x-2} + 3 = 0\]

What is the product of the distinct real solutions?
questions.explanationHtml: Let \(t = \frac{1}{x-2}\). Then \(t^{2} - 4t + 3 = 0 \rightarrow (t-1)(t-3)=0 \rightarrow t=1\) or \(t=3\). \(t=1 \rightarrow x-2=1 \rightarrow x=3\); \(t=3 \rightarrow x-2=\frac{1}{3} \rightarrow x=\frac{7}{3}\). Product \(= 3 \times \frac{7}{3} = 7\).

questions.questionHtml:
\[-3x^{2} + 6x + c = 0\]

In the given equation, \(c\) is a constant. The equation has no real solutions. Which of the following could be the value of \(c\)?
questions.explanationHtml: Discriminant: \(b^{2} - 4ac = 36 - 4(-3)(c) = 36 + 12c\). No real solutions → \(36 + 12c < 0 \rightarrow 12c < -36 \rightarrow c < -3\). Only \(-5\) satisfies.

questions.questionHtml:
\[\begin{cases} y = x^{2} - 2x + 4 \\ y = 2x^{2} - 5x + 3 \end{cases}\]

If \((x_{1}, y_{1})\) and \((x_{2}, y_{2})\) are the two distinct solutions, what is the value of \(x_{1} + x_{2}\)?

\[\begin{cases} y = x^{2} + bx + 9 \\ y = 2x + 3 \end{cases}\]

In the system above, \(b\) is a constant. The graphs of the equations intersect at exactly one point. What is the product of all possible values of \(b\)?
questions.explanationHtml: \(x^{2} + bx + 9 = 2x + 3 \rightarrow x^{2} + (b-2)x + 6 = 0\). Exactly one intersection → discriminant = 0: \((b-2)^{2} - 24 = 0 \rightarrow (b-2)^{2} = 24 \rightarrow b = 2 \pm 2\sqrt{6}\). Product = \((2+2\sqrt{6})(2-2\sqrt{6}) = 4 - 4\cdot6 = 4 - 24 = -20\).
